failures.title: Renault M5R Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: AdBlue/SCR System Crystallisation and Pump Failure - 2018-Present
items.whatHappens: The M5R introduced a more complex Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) system compared to the older K9K. The AdBlue injector and pump are prone to crystallisation, especially in vehicles used primarily for short, urban trips. This leads to warning lights, reduced power (limp mode), and eventually NOx sensor failures.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the AdBlue pump or injector typically costs £400-£900. However, if crystallisation has contaminated the SCR catalyst or caused severe exhaust backpressure, it can damage the turbocharger, necessitating a full M5R replacement.

items.title: Injector Wear and Turbocharger Issues - 2018-Present
items.whatHappens: As a high-pressure common-rail diesel, the M5R's injectors are susceptible to wear and carbon buildup over high mileages. Failing injectors can cause misfires, excessive smoke, and poor fuel economy. If ignored, unburnt fuel can wash the cylinder walls or damage the turbocharger.
items.repairVsReplace: Injector replacement costs £300-£800 per unit. A standalone turbo replacement is £800-£1,500. If the engine has suffered from severe oil starvation or turbo debris ingestion, a full M5R replacement is required.

failures.goodYearsLine: The M5R is the updated Blue dCi revision, meaning post-2018 units have improved emissions hardware compared to the older K9K. However, the added complexity of the AdBlue system means strict adherence to extended oil change intervals (every 12 months or 12,000 miles max) is critical to prevent turbo and injector wear .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the M5R
variants.intro: The M5R is a Specific engine code, but it is frequently confused with the older K9K (the previous generation 1.5 dCi) and the R9M (the 1.6 dCi). The M5R is specifically the 1.5-litre Blue dCi engine equipped with a Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) / AdBlue system, introduced around 2018. Where to find the code: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically near the bell housing, and is also printed on the vehicle’s VIN plate under the bonnet. It is listed on your V5C registration document under "Engine Capacity/Code".

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement M5R - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used M5R is only advisable if accompanied by documented proof that the AdBlue system and injectors have been recently serviced or replaced. Without this history, the risk of inheriting SCR crystallisation or injector wear is high. Explore our used engine options with caution.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the most recommended route for the M5R. A proper reconditioned unit will include tested or replaced injectors, a refreshed turbocharger, and a verified AdBlue/SCR system, permanently resolving the engine's primary weaknesses. View our reconditioned engine services .

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified if your original M5R block has suffered catastrophic turbo failure (debris ingestion) or severe cylinder scoring from injector wash. It allows for the installation of upgraded components during the strip-down. Learn more from our rebuilt engine specialists .

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing through our network ensures your M5R is matched correctly, comes with a minimum 12-month warranty, and can be installed by vetted specialists nationwide via our supply and fit network .
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The M5R is found in the Renault Clio V, Captur II, and Megane IV, which have typical UK values ranging from £7,000 to £16,000. Because a reconditioned replacement can cost upwards of £1,890 fitted, it represents a very small fraction (under 25%) of the vehicle's value. Replacement is highly financially viable and strongly recommended over scrapping for these modern diesel hosts.

items.question: How much does a Renault M5R engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Renault M5R engine typically costs between £1,500 and £2,800 for supply only, or £1,890 to £3,385 fully fitted by an independent specialist . Used units start around £500-£1,200 but carry higher risk without documented AdBlue system history. Full rebuilds addressing injector and turbo wear range from £2,500-£3,800. Labour typically takes 6-9 hours at standard independent rates.

items.question: What is the most common problem with the M5R engine?
items.answer: The most documented issue with the M5R is AdBlue/SCR system crystallisation and pump failure, particularly in vehicles used for short, urban trips. This manifests as warning lights, reduced power (limp mode), and eventually NOx sensor failures. Injector wear and turbocharger issues are also common at higher mileages (80,000+ miles). While AdBlue repairs are routine, ignored injector or turbo failures can lead to catastrophic engine damage requiring full replacement.

items.question: Which Renault models use the M5R engine?
items.answer: The M5R was introduced to meet stricter Euro 6d emissions standards and is fitted to core Renault models from 2018 onwards. It is most commonly found in the Renault Clio V, Captur II, and Megane IV Blue dCi variants. Always verify your V5C, as the older K9K or the larger R9M are not direct plug-and-play swaps due to different ECU mappings and emissions hardware.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned M5R engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned M5R is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the known risks of AdBlue crystallisation and injector wear at higher mileages. A proper reconditioned unit will have tested or replaced injectors, a verified turbocharger, and a cleared/updated AdBlue/SCR system. A used engine is only viable if it comes with documented proof of a recent, comprehensive AdBlue system service and injector health check.

items.answer: The M5R is the updated 1.5-litre Blue dCi engine equipped with a Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) / AdBlue system, introduced around 2018. The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically near the bell housing, and is also printed on the vehicle’s VIN plate. It is explicitly listed on your V5C registration document under "Engine Capacity/Code". If your vehicle is a 2018 or newer Clio, Captur, or Megane diesel, it is highly likely to be the M5R.
